topics.label: Introduction to cancer evolution and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic introduces the lecture framework on cancer evolution and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal selection and cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how genetic mutations and epigenetic modifications drive clonal fitness, selection, and early tumor initiation.

topics.label: Stem cell hierarchy and the cell of origin in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the relationship between normal stem cell hierarchies, cancer stem cells, and the cell of origin using leukemia and colorectal models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion, chronic inflammation, and stromal dependence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how microenvironmental factors, inflammatory signals, and supportive stroma promote tumor progression and sustain established cancers.

topics.label: Technologies for studying tumor evolution and microenvironments
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the experimental, sequencing, and computational methods used to study cancer evolution and spatial interactions.

topics.label: Multifactorial model and synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes the interplay among mutational, cellular, and microenvironmental factors into a comprehensive model of cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic marks the conclusion of the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
